notes.d: This is a grade C (100 HV) washer, for bolts of 6.8 and below and nuts of property class 6 and below.
The hole is large (example: 13.5 for M12), so it does not replace a plain washer for mechanical fastening.

std: DIN 440 R (same dimensions as ISO 7094) · DIN 440 V (square hole)

wedgelock.use: A product that prevents loosening due to vibration by using a pair of washers, each with an inclined cam on the inner face and teeth on the outer face.

notes.d: Fit the two with the cam faces facing each other. Using only one has no effect.
If an equipment drawing specifies a particular manufacturer's product, replace it only with the same product.

std: Manufacturer specification

sqw.use: A washer made by drilling a hole in a thick square steel plate. Used to cover the large holes of foundation anchor bolts and for timber-structure bearings.

notes.d: Foundation anchor bolt holes are often drilled large as a construction allowance, so they are covered with a thick square washer. The size follows the drawing.
If there is a bevel expression (slope, taper, BEVEL), it is handled as a beveled washer.

std: DIN 436 (square washers for timber structures)
ASTM F844 (includes round and other shaped unhardened washers)

sphw.use: A convex spherical washer (C) is paired with a concave conical seat (D · G) so that the bolt does not bend even on an inclined bearing face.

notes.d: C (spherical) and D or G (conical seat) are used as a set. Inserting only one cannot correct the inclination.
The G type has a large seat outside diameter and is used for members with large holes.

std: DIN 6319 (C · D · G)

dti.use: A washer with protrusions, placed under the bolt head or a hardened washer. The gap to which the protrusions are compressed is used to confirm that a high-strength bolt has reached its minimum axial force.

notes.d: The type must match the bolt grade: A325 Type 1 → 325, A490 Type 1 → 490, weathering (Type 3) bolts → 325-3 · 490-3.
Field inspection is judged by the number of protrusions into which the gap gauge does not fit (the acceptance criteria follow the structural connection specification).
For the 490 type, the standard has no gap criterion for mechanical zinc, so confirm the plating specification.

std: Dimensions are per ASME B18.2.6 (original not held)
ASTM F959 (Type 325 · 490, etc., confirmed from the standard document at quotation)

dowel-h.use: A hardened ground pin pressed in to align two parts accurately, as on casings, bearing housings and jigs.

notes.d: A dowel pin is a pin that aligns two parts. The bolts carry the clamping force, and the pin only fixes the position.
The diameter tolerance is m6 (slightly on the large side), so it is pressed into the hole. The hole tolerance follows the design drawing.
Type A is a through-hardened pin and Type B is a surface-hardened pin. If not stated separately, it is quoted as Type A.
A pin placed in a blind hole cannot be pulled out, so where disassembly is needed, choose a parallel pin with internal thread.
Electroplating a hardened pin carries a risk of hydrogen embrittlement, so the default is untreated (rust-preventive oil).
If stainless steel is needed, the martensitic type (C1) is the hardened dowel. 304 and 316 belong to the unhardened parallel pin (ISO 2338).

std: DIN 6325 (replaced by DIN EN ISO 8734)
KS B ISO 8734 (fitting pins)

dowel-u.use: An unhardened parallel pin used for general positioning, hinge shafts and fixing. Stainless steel products are widely used.

notes.d: An unhardened parallel pin is softer than a hardened dowel pin but is easy to machine and replace. For positioning under large loads, use a hardened dowel pin.
Choose the diameter tolerance from m6 (press fit) and h8 (looser side). If not stated, it is quoted as m6 and we will inform you.
The stainless steel material in the standard is A1 (303 family). If 304 is specified, it is handled as an agreed material.
Steel pins can be chosen with black oxide, zinc or phosphate coating. The tolerance is the dimension before coating.

std: DIN 7 (replaced by DIN EN ISO 2338)
KS B ISO 2338 (parallel pins)

dowel-it.use: A dowel pin for blind holes. A pulling bolt can be screwed into the internal thread at the end to disassemble it.

notes.d: Used where the back of the pin is closed, such as split casings and bearing housings. When disassembling, a bolt is screwed into the internal thread to pull it out.
The hardened type (ISO 8735) has a round crown at one end, and the unhardened type (ISO 8733) is chamfered at both ends.
For d1 12 mm the internal thread is M6, and for 16 mm it is M8. The internal thread nominal size may differ from the taper pin (ISO 8736), so match the pulling tool.
If hardening is not stated, it is quoted as the hardened type and confirmation is requested.

std: ISO 8735:1997 (hardened) · ISO 8733:1997 (unhardened)
DIN 7979 (replaced by DIN EN ISO 8733 · 8735)
KS B 1309 (parallel pins with internal thread)

taper.use: A pin that aligns position with a 1:50 taper. It is driven into a reamed hole and knocked out from the large end, so it is used for fits that are disassembled many times.

notes.d: The nominal diameter of a taper pin is the small end diameter. The large end becomes 1 mm thicker for every 50 mm of length (1:50).
The hole is machined through both parts together with a taper reamer. The pin is driven in from the large end and knocked out from the small end.
Type A is ground (Ra 0.8 µm) and Type B is turned (Ra 3.2 µm). If not stated, it is quoted as Type A.
For blind holes or places with frequent repeated disassembly, consider threaded taper pins (internal thread, external thread).

std: DIN 1 (replaced by DIN EN 22339)
KS B 1322 (taper pins)

spring-sl.use: A tubular pin with a longitudinal slot. It is slightly thicker than the hole, so once driven in it clamps itself and does not come out. The most common choice for fixing levers and shafts.

notes.d: The nominal size of a spring pin is the diameter of the hole it fits. The hole is drilled to the nominal diameter with tolerance H12.

The heavy duty type (ISO 8752) is thicker and has a larger shear load, and the light duty type (ISO 13337) is thinner. For ISO 13337, the nominal diameters are set so that pins of different diameters can be nested inside one another or combined with ISO 8752 pins.
Because of the risk of hydrogen embrittlement, spring pins are by default not plated. If corrosion is a concern, choose stainless steel.
Austenitic stainless steel pins have no shear load values in the standard. If the load is important, use steel or martensitic stainless steel.
If only "spring pin" is stated, it is quoted as heavy duty.

std: ISO 8752:2009 (heavy duty) · ISO 13337:2009 (light duty)
KS B ISO 8752 (spring-type straight pins — slotted, heavy duty) · KS B ISO 13337 (slotted, light duty)

cotter.use: A pin inserted into the hole of a castle nut or clevis pin, with its legs spread to prevent it from coming off.

notes.d: The nominal size of a split pin (cotter pin) is the diameter of the hole it fits, not the pin diameter. The actual pin is slightly thinner than the nominal size.
The length l is from under the eye to the end of the short leg. Choose it by adding the allowance for passing through the bolt or pin and spreading the legs.
The nominal size can be chosen from "matching bolt / clevis pin diameter" in the table. If vibration or alternating load applies, one size larger is recommended.
As a rule, a split pin that has been spread and straightened once is not reused.
Inch split pins (ASME B18.8.1) have a different nominal size system from metric. They are received by quotation with reference to the inch dimension table.

std: DIN 94 (replaced by DIN EN ISO 1234)
KS B ISO 1234 (split pins, ISO 1234:1997 IDT)
ASME B18.8.1 (Clevis Pins and Cotter Pins, inch)

taper-th.use: A taper fitting pin for blind holes (internal thread type) or places where it must be pulled out with a nut (external thread type). Used for maintenance of horizontally split casings.

notes.d: The internal thread type is pulled out by screwing a pulling bolt into the internal thread at the large end. It is for blind holes.
The external thread type is pulled out by turning a nut on the thread at the small end, so it is well suited to through holes.
Even for the same nominal size, the internal thread of ISO 8736 may differ from that of the parallel pin (ISO 8735) (example: d1 12 → M8).

std: ISO 8736:1986 (internal thread) · ISO 8737:1986 (external thread)
DIN 7978 (→ ISO 8736) · DIN 7977 (→ ISO 8737) · DIN 258 (original not checked)
KS B 1308 (threaded taper pins)

spring-co.use: A spring pin made by winding thin plate more than 2 turns. It is stronger against shock and fatigue than the slotted type and causes less damage to the hole.

notes.d: When a coiled spring pin is driven in, the whole wound plate contracts evenly, so it damages the hole less.
The plate thickness differs by load class (standard, medium, light). Choose the light duty for soft mating material and the medium duty for hardened mating material.

std: ISO 8750:2007 (standard duty) · ISO 8748:2007 (medium duty) · ISO 8751 (light duty)
KS B ISO 8750 (spring-type straight pins — coiled, standard duty) · KS B ISO 8751 (light duty) · KS B 1345 (spiral pins)

clevis.use: A shaft pin connecting links, actuators and clevises. A split pin or R pin is inserted in the end hole to prevent it from coming off.

notes.d: The split pin hole diameter of a clevis pin is the same as the matching split pin nominal size (example: d 20 → split pin 5).
The washer (ISO 8738) is placed only on the split pin side.
If vibration or alternating load applies, it is recommended to make the split pin one size larger and enlarge the hole as well.

std: ISO 2341:1986 (with head) · ISO 2340:1986 (without head) · ISO 8738:1986 (washer)
ASME B18.8.1 (inch clevis pins)

ipin.use: An inch pin for maintenance of machines built to US standards. Dowel pins come in a standard series and an oversize series for replacement.
std: ASME B18.8.2 (Taper Pins, Dowel Pins, Straight Pins, Grooved Pins, and Spring Pins — Inch Series)

rclip.use: A spring locking pin inserted into the end hole of a clevis pin or shaft without tools to prevent it from coming off. Used where it is attached and removed often.

notes.d: The nominal size of an R pin is the diameter of the shaft hole it is inserted into. Choose it by "matching shaft diameter" in the table.
It can be inserted and removed without tools, which suits places that are disassembled often, but where there is strong vibration a split pin is more secure.

std: DIN 11024 (R pin, type D double wound · type E single) · DIN 11023 (linch pin, original not checked)

grooved.use: A pin made by rolling longitudinal grooves into its body. When driven in, the groove edges press against the hole and hold it, so it is used for fixing nameplates and small parts.

notes.d: Grooved pins have different standard numbers depending on the groove shape (full length, half length, middle, etc.). Please also send the standard number on the drawing.

std: ISO 8739–8745 (grooved pins) · ISO 8746 (round head) · ISO 8747 (countersunk head). ISO 8740 was revised in 2025
ASME B18.8.2 (inch grooved pins)

splittaper.use: A taper pin whose small end is split and spread after driving in so that it does not come out. It appears as a replacement part for machines of Japanese design.

notes.d: The split taper pin is a KS standard item. Quotation is made after confirming the split length and the taper basis from the drawing.

std: KS B 1323 (split taper pins)

ring-ext.use: A C-shaped spring ring fitted in a shaft groove to hold bearings, gears and couplings against axial movement. Pliers are inserted into the lug holes to spread it for fitting.

notes.d: Based on public technical data — only values on which 3 public dimension tables from different manufacturers and distributors agree are listed. Checking against the original standard documents is in progress.

notes.t: Nominal size is the shaft diameter
notes.d: The nominal size of a retaining ring for shafts is the diameter (d1) of the shaft it fits. It is not the groove diameter d2.
The rated load is obtained only if the groove diameter d2, groove width m and clearance n to the shaft end match the table.
A ring that has been spread and removed may change shape, so replacing it with a new one at maintenance is the general practice.

std: DIN 471 (regular and heavy duty types, table based on the 2011-04 edition · current 2026-05 edition)
KS B 1336 C-type retaining rings (for shafts) — whether the dimensions are the same as DIN 471, original not checked
JIS B 2804 C形止め輪 (軸用) — original not checked

ring-int.use: Fitted in a groove in the housing bore to hold the outer ring of a bearing or a part against coming out. Squeezed with pliers for fitting.

notes.d: Based on public technical data — only values on which 3 public dimension tables from different manufacturers and distributors agree are listed. Checking against the original standard documents is in progress.

notes.t: Nominal size is the bore diameter
notes.d: The nominal size of a retaining ring for bores is the housing bore diameter (d1). Choose the same value as the bearing outside diameter.
If only 'snap ring' is stated, we confirm whether it is for shafts or bores. If the lugs are on the outside it is for shafts, and if on the inside it is for bores.

std: DIN 472 (public table based on the 2011 edition · current 2026-05 edition)
KS B 1336 C-type retaining rings (for bores) — original not checked
JIS B 2804 C形止め輪 (穴用) — original not checked

key-par.use: A key of rectangular cross section fitted in the keyways of a shaft and a hub (impeller, coupling, pulley) to transmit torque. It is a finished product with a specified length; if you buy bar stock and cut it yourself, choose key stock.

notes.d: Based on public technical data — only values on which 3 public dimension tables from different manufacturers and distributors agree are listed. Checking against the original standard documents is in progress.
b×h is set for each shaft diameter range. Combinations outside the table are changed to a quotation for cutting key stock to fit.
Type A has rounded ends (end mill keyway) and Type B has square ends (side cutter keyway). If not stated, it is quoted as Type A and confirmed.

notes.t: Fit is set by the keyway tolerance
notes.d: Tight, normal and sliding fits are determined not by the key but by the shaft and hub keyway tolerances (P9 · N9 · JS9 · H9 · D10).
If the equipment drawing has separate height and length tolerances, it is quoted as a drawing item made to order.

std: DIN 6885-1 (high type, current 2021-11 edition · public table based on the 1968 edition). DIN 6885-2 (high type for machine tools) · -3 (low type) are quoted
KS B 1311 Sunk keys and keyways · KS B 1313 Sliding keys — whether the dimensions are the same as DIN 6885-1, original not checked
JIS B 1301 — original not checked
ISO/R 773 was withdrawn (1998)
mats: Carbon steel C45 (cold drawn, equivalent to S45C)

kmnut.use: A round nut with 4 slots around its circumference that presses and fixes a bearing inner ring or adapter sleeve onto the shaft. A tongue of the MB lock washer is bent into a slot to prevent loosening.

notes.d: A single KM number determines the thread, outside diameter and width. KM8 = M40×1.5.
An MB lock washer comes with a KM nut. The washer is single-use (1-time), so it is replaced together at maintenance.

std: ISO 2982-2:2013 (only the symbol definitions checked against the original, dimension table not checked)
DIN 981:2009-06 (current)
KS B 2004 Locknuts, washers and stoppers for rolling bearings (ISO 2982-2:2013 MOD)
JIS B 1554 (AN designation) — original not checked

mbw.use: A washer used together with a KM locknut. The inner tongue is bent into the shaft keyway and one outer tab into a nut slot to prevent the nut from loosening.

notes.d: Based on public technical data — only values on which 3 public dimension tables from different manufacturers and distributors agree are listed. Checking against the original standard documents is in progress.
A tab that has been bent is not straightened and reused. If the nut has been loosened, replace the washer with a new one.
There must be a shaft groove for the inner tongue to enter. If there is no groove, consider another locking method (stopper, precision nut).

std: ISO 2982-2:2013 (only the symbol definitions checked against the original)
DIN 5406:2011-04 (current)
JIS B 1554 (AW designation) — original not checked

ering.use: An E-shaped retaining washer pushed sideways into a shaft groove. It need not be slid to the shaft end, so it is used on small shafts.

notes.t: Nominal size is the groove diameter
notes.d: E-ring 6 is for a groove diameter of 6 mm, and the shaft diameter is 7–9 mm.
An E-ring cannot take a large axial force. For bearing retention, use a C-type retaining ring for shafts.

std: DIN 6799 (current 2026-05 edition · table from public material of the 2011 · 2017 editions)
KS B 1337 E-type retaining rings
JIS B 2804 E形止め輪 — original not checked

key-wood.use: A half-moon shaped key that fits in a circular-arc keyway of the shaft. Used on small shafts or tapered shaft ends.
std: DIN 6888 (current 2022-03 edition · table from a public summary of the 1956 edition)
KS B 1311 (includes half-moon keys)
ASME B17.2 (inch, number designation example: No. 606)
ISO 3912 withdrawn
mats: Carbon steel C45 (cold drawn, equivalent to S45C)

key-inch.use: A key for inch shafts (US-made pumps and motors). The square key size is set for each shaft diameter range.

notes.t: Beware of mixing inch and metric
notes.d: A 1/4 in key (6.35 mm) does not fit a metric 6 mm keyway. Check the shaft unit first.

std: ASME B17.1 Keys and Keyseats (original not checked)
mats: Carbon steel C45 (cold drawn, equivalent to S45C)

keystock.use: Bar stock drawn to a parallel key cross section (b×h). It is cut to length on site to make keys.

notes.d: Unlike a finished key (parallel key) with a specified length, bar stock has no end machining. If end rounding is needed, order a finished key.

std: DIN 6880:2011 (key steel — dimensions, tolerances, mass)
The cross section b×h is the KS B 1311 key cross section (original not checked)
ASME B17.1 (inch cross sections)
mats: Carbon steel C45 (cold drawn, equivalent to S45C)

tabw.use: A tab of the washer is bent over a part edge or into a hole, and another is bent against the face of the nut or bolt head to keep it from turning.

notes.d: A tab that has been bent is not reused. If disassembled, replace it with a new one.

std: DIN 93 · DIN 463 · DIN 432 (all withdrawn without a successor standard)

ring-misc.use: Includes snap rings made of round wire, lugged rings with lugs projecting outward, inch standard rings, and spiral rings made of overlapped winding.

notes.d: Rings for inch shafts and bores have different groove dimensions from metric rings and are not interchanged.

std: DIN 7993 (withdrawn → DIN 9925 · DIN 9926:2016-11) · DIN 983 (lugged, for shafts) · DIN 984 (lugged, for bores)
KS B 1069 Grip rings
ASME B18.27 (inch tapered and reduced cross section rings) · ASME B27.6 (spiral)

key-gib.use: A key with a sloped top surface and a head at one end. It is driven in to fix and pulled out by the head. Used in old equipment.

notes.d: The head protrudes from the rotating shaft, so check the guard.

std: DIN 6887 (current 1968-04 edition)
ASME B17.1 (inch gib head)

ilocknut.use: Bearing nuts (N · AN series) for inch shafts and adapter sleeves, and mating washers (W series). They appear in maintenance of old US-made pumps and blowers.

notes.d: Even for the same 'AN 08', a metric thread (M40×1.5) means KM8, and an inch thread means the inch series.

std: ANSI/ABMA 8.2 (dimensions original not checked)
